name: Tiefenbachklamm
kurzbeschreibung: Tiefenbachklamm between Brandenberg and Kramsach: spectacular 4 km gorge trail along the Brandenberger Ache with viewing platform and timber floating history.
beschreibung:
Overview

The wildly romantic Tiefenbachklamm is situated in the Tyrolean Unterinntal between the municipalities of Brandenberg and Kramsach in the district of Kufstein. Carved by the rushing torrents of the Brandenberger Ache, the gorge ranks among the scenic highlights of Tyrolean canyon hikes. Over millions of years, the mountain water carved deeply into the fractured dolomite rock, fashioning an archaic canyon landscape of bizarrely eroded rock formations, emerald-green rock pools, and foaming whirlpool basins. The secured Triftsteig trail, approximately four kilometres long, offers spectacular glimpses into the untamed power of Alpine torrents.

Geology & Timber Floating History

The formation of the gorge dates back to the tectonic uplift of the Limestone Alps and the erosive force of meltwater slicing through narrow rock fissures down into the Inntal valley. Beyond its scenic grandeur, the Tiefenbachklamm looks back on more than 500 years of industrial heritage: the renowned Brandenberger Holztrift (timber floating). First documented in 1412, loggers transported felled tree trunks from inaccessible mountain forests down to the valley on the torrents of the Ache for centuries. The timber was vital fuel for the salt works (Saline) in Hall in Tirol, the copper smelting works in Brixlegg, and the silver mines in Schwaz. To maneuver the logs through narrow gorges, log-drivers built bold wooden walkways directly onto vertical rock faces. The final historic timber drive took place in 1966, after which modern road haulage replaced river log driving. Today, an elaborately secured hiking trail traverses the gorge across footbridges and rock-cut tunnels. The highlight is a boldly engineered Aussichtsplattform (viewing platform) halfway along: the steel grating structure juts freely out over the canyon, providing a breathtaking view looking straight down into the boiling waters of the Ache.

Visit & Arrival

The Tiefenbachklamm is open seasonally during daylight hours from early May to late October. During the winter months (November to April) and in times of torrential rain or flooding, the trail is officially closed for safety reasons. Access to the canyon hiking trail is completely free of charge (€0.00 admission). Arrival by public transport: Take the ÖBB train to Bahnhof Brixlegg, then take bus line 605 to Kramsach. During the summer months (July to early September), the free „Klamm-Express“ shuttle bus runs every 20 minutes from the large Wittberg car park in Kramsach directly to the gorge entrance. By car: Inntalautobahn A12, exit Kramsach; it is strongly recommended to park at the free Wittberg car park (former Sonnwendjochbahn) and take the shuttle bus to the trailhead (only approx. 17 short-stay paid parking spots are available directly at the entrance). An alternative entrance from above is via Brandenberg/Aschau with parking at the Jausenstation.

Tips

The gorge trail is natural in character with rock-hewn steps, gravel, and timber planks, making it not barrier-free (unsuitable for wheelchairs and strollers); sure-footed hiking footwear with good grip is mandatory. For families with children up to ten years of age, safety harness tethering is recommended: specialized safety harnesses with carabiner leashes can be hired for a small deposit at the Jausenstation Tiefenbachklamm or from Sport Ossi in Kramsach. At the upper end of the gorge, the rustic Jausenstation Tiefenbachklamm invites visitors to stop for refreshments with its large playground and sunny terrace.
preis: Kostenlos frei begehbar (Klamm-Express-Shuttlebus im Sommer gratis)
